info.title: Polpo API
info.description: REST API for Polpo — an AI agent that manages teams of AI coding agents. Manage tasks, missions, agents, playbooks, skills, notifications, and approvals. For conversational interaction, use the OpenAI-compatible POST /v1/chat/completions endpoint.

bearerAuth.description: API key passed as a Bearer token. Configure via the apiKeys field in polpo.json or the POLPO_API_KEY environment variable.

connectors.description: Connector ids the run may use (each account of an app is its own connector, e.g. gmail-2), or "none". Absent: every connector the agent has.

connectorTools.description: Per connector id: "*" or the server's raw tool names. Narrows the agent's own connectorTools.

allowedTools.description: Built-in tools or patterns (read, bash, browser_*), not connector tools. Narrows the agent's allowedTools (or its default tools).

agent.description: An existing agent plays the role: its name, optionally @version or @draft (judge-bot@1.2.0)

model.description: Or a model + engine block, as an agent's (run as an ephemeral agent): the model (provider:id)

engine.description: The block's engine, as agent.engine: "polpo", { harness, … } or { type: "cli", cli, account?, model? }

fastPath.description: Answered without the model (an obvious "go to X")

titleHighlights.description: Matched [start, end) ranges in the title

snippet.description: The matching passage (secrets masked) and its matched [start, end) ranges

url.description: Dashboard route that opens the item

meta.description: Type details: agent, status, messageId, author, columns…

message.description: handoff: the message for a new Polpo chat

auto.description: true: the dashboard does it at once (navigation, view-only commands); false: a button the person clicks

until.description: When the event log took over

before.description: Deliveries counted before the event log existed: totals only, no entry in the log. The other counts are the event log's.

payload.description: The redacted payload (JSON), or a redacted text preview; capped at 4 KB

headers.description: Safe headers only (never a signature or an authorization)

get.summary: Check if Polpo is configured and initialized

post.summary: Save config and initialize the orchestrator

409.description: Already initialized or initialization in progress

post.summary: Configure the first instance auth admin

409.description: Instance auth is already configured

get.summary: List all LLM providers with credential status
List all available models, optionally filtered by provider

post.summary: Send user input for an OAuth flow

get.summary: List models for a specific provider

post.summary: Save an API key for a provider

delete.summary: Remove an API key for a provider
Disconnect a provider — removes API key and OAuth profiles

post.description: Polpo's primary conversational interface. Send messages in OpenAI format, receive responses in OpenAI format. Polpo runs its full 37-tool agentic loop internally — you describe what you need, Polpo handles the rest. Supports streaming (SSE) and non-streaming modes.

role.description: Message role. System messages are appended as additional context (Polpo has its own system prompt).

url.description: Base64 data URL for a persistent image attachment

content.description: Message content — plain string or array of content parts (text / image_url)

stream.description: If true, returns an SSE stream of OpenAI-format chunks. If false, returns a complete response.

model.description: Ignored. Polpo uses its configured orchestrator model (or the agent's model in agent-direct mode).

agent.description: Target a specific agent by name for direct conversation. Uses the agent's own model, system prompt, and coding tools instead of the orchestrator. Omit to talk to the orchestrator (default).

focus.description: What the summary should pay particular attention to.

compact.description: Compact the session's context now instead of answering: the earlier conversation is summarized (as when the window fills) and the checkpoint is saved for the next turns. Requires x-session-id of an existing session. Returns { compaction } without calling the model for an answer.

200.description: Chat completion response (non-streaming). When stream=true, returns text/event-stream with OpenAI-format chunks ending with data: [DONE].

400.description: Invalid request (missing messages or no project available)

schema.description: If `true`, returns a slim projection: drops `outcomes`, `result.stdout/stderr` (keeps `result.assessment`; a failed task gets `failure`: its reason in a line, `retryable`, `kind`), `expectations`, `metrics`, `maxRetries`, `runs` (replaced by `lastRun`: engine, model, computer of the latest run, and `cost`: the total of every run `{ usd, tokens, runs, partial? }`), and truncates `description` to 200 chars. Default `false` — full record for backwards compat with the SDK and web UI. Bandwidth-sensitive clients (mobile) should opt in.

parameters.description: If `true`, returns a slim projection: drops `outcomes`, `result.stdout/stderr` (keeps `result.assessment`; a failed task gets `failure`: its reason in a line, `retryable`, `kind`), `expectations`, `metrics`, `maxRetries`, `runs` (replaced by `lastRun`: engine, model, computer of the latest run, and `cost`: the total of every run `{ usd, tokens, runs, partial? }`), and truncates `description` to 200 chars. Default `false` — full record for backwards compat with the SDK and web UI. Bandwidth-sensitive clients (mobile) should opt in.
parameters.name: summary

schema.description: Alias for `summary=true`. Returns the slim projection (id, title, status, phase, assignTo, group, missionId, dependsOn, retries, timestamps, optional slim assessment, descriptionPreview, lastRun, cost (every run's total), failure, toolScope).

parameters.description: Alias for `summary=true`. Returns the slim projection (id, title, status, phase, assignTo, group, missionId, dependsOn, retries, timestamps, optional slim assessment, descriptionPreview, lastRun, cost (every run's total), failure, toolScope).
parameters.name: slim

schema.description: Page size (default 50, max 200). Presence triggers the paginated response shape `{ tasks, nextCursor, hasMore }`.

parameters.description: Page size (default 50, max 200). Presence triggers the paginated response shape `{ tasks, nextCursor, hasMore }`.
parameters.name: limit

schema.description: ISO timestamp from a previous page's `nextCursor`. Returns tasks with `updated_at < cursor`. Ignored when `q` is set.

parameters.description: ISO timestamp from a previous page's `nextCursor`. Returns tasks with `updated_at < cursor`. Ignored when `q` is set.
parameters.name: cursor

schema.description: Full-text search across task title and description. Uses SQLite FTS5 with prefix matching. When set, results are ranked by relevance and `cursor` is ignored.

parameters.description: Full-text search across task title and description. Uses SQLite FTS5 with prefix matching. When set, results are ranked by relevance and `cursor` is ignored.
parameters.name: q

schema.description: Only tasks updated at or after this time: an ISO date/time (`2026-11-21T08:00:00Z`) or a duration back from now (`30m`, `24h`, `7d`, `2w`, `PT24H`). 400 INVALID_SINCE otherwise.

parameters.description: Only tasks updated at or after this time: an ISO date/time (`2026-11-21T08:00:00Z`) or a duration back from now (`30m`, `24h`, `7d`, `2w`, `PT24H`). 400 INVALID_SINCE otherwise.
parameters.name: updatedSince

200.description: List of tasks. Returns `{ tasks, nextCursor, hasMore }` when `limit`/`cursor`/`q` is set, otherwise `Task[]` for backwards compat.

304.description: Not modified — client has the current list per ETag

400.description: `updatedSince` is neither an ISO date/time nor a duration (INVALID_SINCE)
dependsOn names a task that does not exist (UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY), or toolScope asks for a connector or tool the agent does not have (INVALID_TOOL_SCOPE)

409.description: A task with this title already exists among active tasks

200.description: Task details. `runs`: where and with what each run executed (engine polpo / claude-code / codex / opencode, model, auth kind, computer, sandbox, egress, harness session, cost, budget, status, duration), newest last. `result.stderr` of a failed task is its labelled reason (a harness error says what to change); `result.retryable: false`: it was not retried automatically (model not enabled for the account, credentials refused). `failure` sums it up: `{ reason, retryable, kind }` (kind: model_access, auth, budget, killed, assessment, error). `cost`: what every run of the task cost in all (first run, retries, continuations, directions): `{ usd, harnessUsd, modelUsd, tokens, runs, lastRunUsd, byEngine, perRun, partial, recoveredUsd? }` — `partial: true` when older runs were dropped (a task keeps its latest 20) and could not be recovered from the usage records.

400.description: toolScope asks for a connector or tool the agent does not have (INVALID_TOOL_SCOPE)

202.description: Direction queued for the active or next task runner

409.description: Task state does not permit this direction

schema.description: If `true`, returns a slim projection: drops the (potentially large) `data` JSON blob and the full `prompt`, adds derived `taskCount` and truncated `promptPreview`. Default `false` for backwards compat — the web UI parses `mission.data` directly for now. Use this from mobile / bandwidth-sensitive clients.

Default `false` for backwards compat — the web UI parses `mission.data` directly for now. Use this from mobile / bandwidth-sensitive clients.

parameters.description: Alias for `summary=true`. Returns a slim projection (id, name, status, schedule, deadline, endDate, qualityThreshold, budgetUsd, pauseReason, owner, cost, timestamps, taskCount, promptPreview).

200.description: List of missions, each with a compact `cost` (usd, tokens, runs, partial, budgetUsd, overBudget)

304.description: Not modified — client has the current list per ETag

budgetUsd.description: Spending limit in USD for the whole mission (all its tasks' runs). When reached, no new task starts (running ones finish) and the mission pauses until the budget is raised or cleared.

400.description: A task's toolScope asks for a connector or tool its agent does not have (INVALID_TOOL_SCOPE)

200.description: Mission details, with `cost`: what its tasks' recorded runs cost (usd, tokens, runs, harnessUsd vs modelUsd, byAgent, byEngine, partial when older runs were dropped) against `budgetUsd` (remainingUsd, budgetUsed, overBudget), or agentBudgetCapUsd when it has no budget

budgetUsd.description: Spending limit in USD for the whole mission; null clears it. Raising or clearing it lets a mission paused by its budget go on.

400.description: A task's toolScope asks for a connector or tool its agent does not have (INVALID_TOOL_SCOPE)

404.description: Checkpoint not found or not active

schema.description: If `true`, returns a slim projection: only the identity bits the list rows render (displayName, title, avatar, company, email) plus pre-computed `capabilities` counts. Drops `allowedTools`, `allowedPaths`, `skills`, `mcpServers`, `systemPrompt`, `reasoning`, `browserProfile`, `emailAllowedDomains`, `suggestions`, and the bulky `identity.responsibilities/bio/personality/tone/timezone`. Default `false` for backwards compat.

get.description: The agent as production runs it, with `versioning` (production version, latest, draft state). `view=draft`: its draft (working copy) instead, as the dashboard edits it.
Published versions, newest first (without their config: GET …/versions/{version} has it), with the production pointer and the draft's state.
A published version with its full config snapshot (read-only). `draft` and `production` are accepted too.

Per-field changes and a git-style unified diff of the serialized config between two refs: a version (1.2.0), `production` or `draft`. `to` defaults to `draft`; `from` defaults to the latest version for the draft, else the version before `to`.

delete.description: Throw away the draft's unpublished changes (production is not touched).

post.description: A draft is based on the version production ran when it started. After a rollback or deploy moved production elsewhere the draft is stale (`versioning.draft.stale`): this applies its own changes over what production runs now (or drops it when nothing is left to change).

Publish the draft as a new immutable version: the suggested bump (patch for text/prompt/identity, minor for added tools/skills/connectors/settings, major for an engine or model change or removed tools/skills/connectors) unless `bump` or `version` says otherwise. Publishing does not deploy: `deploy: true` also deploys it to production.

deploy.description: Also deploy it to production (through the deploy gate when the agent has required suites)

wait.description: With deploy: wait for the required suites to finish (default: the deploy is returned pending)

200.description: Published (and deployed, or its deploy pending / blocked by the required suites: `deployStatus`, `gate`; without deploy, `check`: the publish checks started)

409.description: No draft changes, the version exists, or the draft is stale (rebase or discard it)

post.description:
Move the production pointer to a published version: everything that runs the agent without a pinned version (chats, tasks, missions, schedules, channels, MCP, Polpo) uses it from its next run; runs in flight keep theirs. Recorded in the deploy history with who, when, from → to and the note.

**Deploy gate**: when the agent has required suites (`gate.required`), they run against the version first (trigger `deploy`) and the request answers `202` with the gate pending (`GET …/deploy-gates/{id}`, events `agent:gate`): production moves only when every one passes; otherwise the deploy is blocked and recorded in the history (`action: blocked`). `wait: true` waits for the verdict (`200` deployed, `409` `GATE_BLOCKED`). `override: { reason }` (admins only) deploys at once anyway, recording which gates had failed.

override.description: Deploy even if the required suites fail (or without running them): admins only, the reason is recorded

wait.description: Wait for the required suites (default: return the deploy pending, 202)

200.description: Deployed: the history entry, `status: deployed`, its `gate` when the suites verified it (or an override)

202.description: Pending: the required suites are running (`status: pending`, `gate`)

403.description: An override by someone who is not an admin

409.description: Blocked by the required suites (`GATE_BLOCKED`, with `data.gate`), or another version is being verified

get.description: The agent's deploy gates, newest first: the required suites run against a version before a deploy (trigger deploy / api-update) or when it is published (publish). Each: status (running — in verifica —, passed, blocked, failed, override, cancelled, errored), progress, each suite's run, pass rate, score, the reasons it failed and its failed cases, the override.
A gate with its progress (while running), each required suite's run and verdict, the deploy (or block) it led to. `wait` (seconds, up to 55): wait for it to finish first.

post.description: Stop a gate that is running: its suite runs are cancelled and nothing is deployed (production is unchanged).

409.description: Not running

post.description: Deploy a gate's version although its required suites did not pass (or are still running: they are cancelled). Admins only; the reason is mandatory. The deploy history records the override: who, when, the reason and which gates had failed.

409.description: Already deployed

post.description: Deploy the version production ran before the current one (or `to`). A rollback is a deploy: it appears in the history with its diff. It is never gated by the required suites (it must always work); a verification in flight is cancelled.

409.description: Nothing to roll back to

get.description: Every move of the production pointer, newest first: when, who, from → to, note, rollback marker; deploys the required suites blocked (`action: blocked`). Each entry verified by a deploy gate carries `gate` (status, the suites and their runs, what failed, the override). `diff=true` adds each deploy's diff (per-field changes and a unified diff of the config).
A deploy (or rollback) and the git-style diff between the version it replaced and the one it deployed.

post.description: Runs checks of everything the agent has at its disposal: engine and model (a minimal real request, a few tokens), tools, connectors, vault references (names only), skills, computer and sandbox, channels, versioning; `smoke` (only when listed) runs a tiny real chat turn that calls one harmless tool. Each check returns pass / warn / fail with its items and a fix when there is one. The run is kept in the agent's history.

checks.description: Which checks (default: all but smoke, the live run that costs a real turn)

target.description: production (default), draft, or a published version (1.2.0)

startComputer.description: Start a stopped remote computer to test it (it may cost)

smokePrompt.description: The smoke run's message (default: call one harmless tool)

get.description: The agent's test runs, newest first, with each check's result, the target and version tested and when.

post.description: Applies a one-click fix a check offered: `grant-connector-access` adds the agent to the connector's access list (the agent names the connector's tools in allowedTools but cannot see them).

get.description: The agent's test and eval suites (cases, datasets, mocks), by name.

post.description: Creates a suite: { name, description?, defaultMode (none | tools | model | all, default all), mocks?, cases: [{ name, input: { kind: chat | task, message, history?, context? }, mode?, mocks?: { tools?: [{ tool, when?, response?, error?, delayMs?, times? }], model?: { turns: [{ text?, toolCalls? }] }, unmockedTools? }, assertions: [...], dataset?, budgets? }], datasets?: [{ name, rows }] }, or { yaml } with the same in YAML. Ids are made from names when missing.

409.description: A suite with this id exists

get.description: The suite; ?format=yaml returns { yaml, revision } (the YAML view).

put.description: Replaces the suite (validated), or creates it. Send `revision` (the one you edited) to refuse the save when someone changed it meanwhile (409). Body: the suite, or { yaml, revision? }.

409.description: Changed meanwhile

delete.description: Deletes the suite (its past runs stay in the history).

post.description: Imports rows from CSV (first line: the column names; quotes, comma, semicolon or tab) or JSON (a list of objects, or { rows }) into a new dataset, or replaces / appends the rows of the dataset `id`. Cases use a dataset with `dataset: <id>` and {{row.column}} in their input, mocks and assertions.

coerce.description: CSV: numbers and booleans from text (default true)

post.description: Runs the suite (or `caseIds`) against the agent at `target` (production, draft, 1.2.0), each case a real chat turn through the agent's own path with its mocks: mode all runs offline (scripted model, mocked tools), tools mocks the tools (real model), model scripts the model (real tools), none is live. A run that uses real tools needs `allowRealTools: true` (403 otherwise); approvals are never given. `overrides` change the agent for this run only. Returns the run (running, or finished with `wait: true`); poll GET /agents/{name}/suite-runs/{runId}.

target.description: production (default), draft, or a published version (1.2.0)

mode.description: Run every case in this mode (default: each case's own): none, tools, model, all

overrides.description: Per-run changes to the agent (model, reasoning, engine, instructions, allowedTools, maxTurns): this run only

wait.description: Wait for the run to finish (default false: the run is returned running)

repetitions.description: Run every case this many times (mean, stddev and flakiness per case; default the suite's evals.repetitions, 1)

baselineRunId.description: Compare with this run instead of the suite's baseline

regressionTolerance.description: A score or pass-rate change within this is not a regression (default the suite's, 0.05)

allowRealTools.description: Confirm a run that uses real tools (modes none / model, or unmocked tools run for real): side effects are possible; approvals are never given

record.description: Record: run the cases live (real model and tools; needs allowRealTools and an admin) and save each one's exchange as its cassette (secrets redacted); the cases replay it from then on

get.description: The suite's finished runs over time, oldest first: pass rate, overall score, mean per scorer, cost, latency, regressions versus the baseline; and the same by version (production's version, a published one, or draft).

The run marked as the suite's baseline (summary, without traces), or null. Without a marked baseline, a new run is compared with the suite's policy (evals.baseline: previous — default —, production or none).

put.summary: Mark a run as the baseline
put.description: Marks a finished run of the suite as its baseline: every new run is compared with it (deltas per case and per scorer, regressions and improvements). The previous mark is removed; a marked run is never dropped from the history.

delete.description: Removes the suite's baseline mark: new runs are compared by the suite's policy (the previous run by default).

get.description: Runs, newest first, without traces (each case's status, failed assertions, cost, duration); ?suite= one suite, ?benchmark= one benchmark, ?full=true with traces.
The run with each case's assertions (pass / fail, message, expected, actual, diff) and trace (model turns, tool calls with arguments and results, mocks hit, approvals, usage).

get.summary: Compare a run with a baseline
get.description: The run compared with ?baseline=<runId>, or with its suite's baseline now (the marked run, else the suite's policy): pass rate, score, cost and duration deltas; per case and per scorer the change (regressed, improved, unchanged, new, removed) beyond ?tolerance= (default the suite's, 0.05). null when there is nothing to compare with.

post.description: Asks the suite's reviewer (evals.reviewer, or `reviewer` here: an agent or a model + engine block; default Polpo) to explain a finished run, in a chat turn without tools: a summary, what failed or regressed and why, and suggested fixes (instruction and tool changes, or the test itself). Stored on the run as `review` (Markdown); costs tokens.

409.description: No model, or the review failed

post.description: Stops a running run: cases not started are skipped; running ones stop before their next model call or tool.

Appends cases (validated like a saved suite's; an id already used gets a new one) and the datasets they use: e.g. the generated cases a person accepted. `revision` refuses the save when the suite changed meanwhile (409).

The suite's generator (or `generator` here; default Polpo) proposes rows for a case's dataset (its columns kept; edge and adversarial values included), or a first dataset for a case that uses {{row.x}}, in a chat turn without tools. Nothing is saved: add the rows you keep (datasets/import or a save). Costs tokens.

409.description: No model

post.description: The suite's generator (or `generator` here: an agent or a model + engine block; default Polpo, in a chat turn without tools) proposes cases from the agent's instructions, tools, skills and connectors (and a brief, sample chats): input, mocks, assertions, scorers and dataset rows, including edge cases and adversarial / prompt-injection ones. Each proposal is validated and returned with its rationale; nothing is saved — accept the ones you keep with POST …/suites/{id}/cases. Costs tokens.

suiteId.description: The suite the cases are for (ids kept unique)

sessionIds.description: Real chats with the agent to draw from

style.description: contract (default): scripted model turns and tool mocks (offline); tools: the real model with mocked tools

allOf.description: Who writes them (default the suite's generator, else Polpo): a chat turn of that agent or model + engine block

409.description: No model, or the generation failed

post.summary: A case from a real chat or task
post.description: Turns a chat session with the agent (`sessionId`, the user message at `messageIndex`, default the last one) or a task run (`taskId`, its activity) into a case and its cassette: the exchange is replayed offline (mode all) and the same tool calls are checked in order. Secrets are redacted from the cassette. The case is added to the suite.

get.description: The recording a case replays (every model turn and tool call with its arguments and result, secrets redacted), or null when it was never recorded.

post.description: Runs the case live — the agent's real model and real tools: side effects are possible, so it needs `allowRealTools: true` and an admin (403 otherwise) — and saves its exchange as the case's cassette (secrets redacted: vault values, auth headers, tokens). The case then replays it offline. Calls turned into mocks stay pinned. Returns the recording run (finished with `wait: true`).

403.description: Not confirmed, or not an admin

get.description: The recordings its cases replay, newest first, without their calls (tools, how many calls and turns, redactions, where they were recorded).
A recording with every model turn and tool call (arguments, result, error, edited, turned into a mock).

patch.description: Per recorded call: a new `response` (and `isError`), `delete`, or `markAsMock` (the call becomes a tool mock of its case, kept on re-recording). `revision` refuses an edit over a newer one (409).

markAsMock.description: Turn the call into a tool mock of its case (a re-recording keeps it pinned)

409.description: Changed meanwhile

delete.description: Deletes the recording: the cases pointing at it block their tool calls until they are recorded again.

get.summary: Computer provider webhooks: each provider's status
get.description: Per provider (daytona, e2b): the signing secret is set, registered (E2B), the URL to give the provider, the last event, the counters (they follow the event log), the last problem since it was configured, and the state (receiving / configured / not-configured). `waitingNote`: configured but no delivery ever arrived. Never a secret.

Every delivery the provider sent (the last 200), newest first: accepted (a computer was checked at its provider), ignored (not about one of this instance's computers, a duplicate, an event Polpo does not act on), rejected (signature, replay, size, rate, not configured) or error (Polpo could not apply it). Without payloads (GET /{provider}/events/{id}). `counts`: entries kept per outcome.

schema.description: Comma-separated outcomes: accepted, ignored, rejected, error
